layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Given a video and a set of input object masks, an om-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nimatte method aims to decompose the video into semanti-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cally meaningful layers containing individual objects along

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with their associated effects, such as shadows and reflec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions. Existing omnimatte methods assume a static back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground or accurate pose and depth estimation and produce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poor decompositions when these assumptions are violated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Furthermore, due to the lack of generative prior on natu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ral videos, existing methods cannot complete dynamic oc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cluded regions. We present a novel generative layered video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decomposition framework to address the omnimatte prob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lem. Our method does not assume a stationary scene or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: require camera pose or depth information and produces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clean, complete layers, including convincing completions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of occluded dynamic regions. Our core idea is to train a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video diffusion model to identify and remove scene effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: caused by a specific object. We show that this model can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be fnetuned from an existing video inpainting model with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a small, carefully curated dataset, and demonstrate high-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quality decompositions and editing results for a wide range

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of casually captured videos containing soft shadows, glossy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reflections, splashing water, and more.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Natural videos typically intertwine complex signals about

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our dynamic world, such as camera motion, articulated ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ject movement, intricate scene effects, and time-varying in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teraction between objects. Mid-level representations that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *Work done while Yao-Chih was an intern at Google DeepMind.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model this complexity are vital for intuitive interaction and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: editing of video content. One such representation is a de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composition of video into a set of semantically meaningful,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semi-transparent layers, typically with one layer for each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foreground object and the background. The utility of layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in creating visual effects has fueled interest in generating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: them from casually-captured video.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Omnimatte [19, 29, 35–37, 47] methods produce se-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mantically meaningful layers that contain individual ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jects along with their associated effects, such as shadows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and reflections. To infer the complex space-time correla-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions between objects and their effects, existing methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rely heavily on restrictive assumptions such as a stationary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background or accurate camera and depth estimation. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods fail when these assumptions are violated. Further-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more, existing methods cannot complete occluded regions,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limiting their potential applications (Fig. 2).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this work, we present a novel generative layered video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decomposition framework that overcomes previous limita-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions by leveraging the strong generative prior of a pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained video diffusion model [7]. The video prior serves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two purposes. First, the model's internal features reveal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: connections between objects and their effects (Fig. 5) that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be exposed through finetuning, similar to recent works

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that apply the internal features of video diffusion models for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analysis tasks [22, 44]. Second, the model can directly com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plete occluded areas in the layer decomposition, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dynamic regions. This prior is a key factor that enables our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method to dispense with the ad-hoc, limited priors of previ-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ous works [19, 29, 36, 47] and the restrictions they place on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the input video.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, existing video inpainting models are not di-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rectly applicable to the omnimatte task — because they

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inpaint only the region indicated by a binary mask, they

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lack the flexibility to remove associated effects outside of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the mask region (Fig. 3). Instead, we finetune the video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inpainting model to create an object-effect-removal model,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and apply it as a core component of a layer-decomposition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system (Fig. 4). The model produces a “clean-plate" RGB

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background layer and initialization for the foreground lay-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ers. The final RGBA foreground layers are optimized to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reconstruct the input video while remaining sparse. Since

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the pretrained model's features already connect objects and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their effects, a small, carefully curated dataset of real and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: synthetic examples of object-effect associations is sufficient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for finetuning.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our method advances video layer decomposition in two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: directions: (i) it operates on casual videos where previous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods fail, without relying on a stationary background or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: camera poses, and (ii) it generates realistic, dynamic lay-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ers for both fully occluded regions and regions partially oc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cluded by shadows or reflections. These capabilities unlock

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: various creative editing tasks such as object removal, move-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 2. Limitations of existing Omnimatte methods. Om-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nimatte methods [19, 29, 36, 47] rely on restrictive motion as-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sumptions, such as stationary background, resulting in dynamic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background elements becoming entangled with foreground object

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layers. Furthermore, these methods lack a generative and seman-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tic prior for completing occluded pixels and accurately associating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects with their corresponding objects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 3. Limitations of inpainting models for object removal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While video inpainting models (e.g., [66]) can complete plausible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background pixels in the input mask region, they preserve the re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moved objects' shadows and reflections outside the mask.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment retiming, and foreground stylization (Fig. 1). We will

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: release the dataset of real and synthetic layered videos used

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to finetune the video inpainting model.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Transparent Images and Matting. Transparent (RGBA)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images and videos are widely used in various applica-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions, including rotoscoping and visual effects synthesis.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The matting problem [40, 50] aims to extract foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: RGBAs and background layers from the given images or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: videos. In the visual effects industry, this layer decom-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: position is traditionally achieved by green-screen chroma

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: keying, requiring complex filming setups and manual post-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: processing [34]. Deep learning methods [24, 26, 30, 52] ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proach this problem by training on large-scale alpha matte

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: groundtruth [26, 30]. These studies focus on estimating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine-level alpha mattes for foregrounds but cannot capture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the correlated effects. Recent advancements [62] have en-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: abled text-to-RGBA image generation with plausible effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by finetuning Stable Diffusion [42] on a transparent image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset. Nonetheless, decomposing videos into layers with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect association is a different problem domain and remains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: under-explored.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Video Layer Decomposition. Decomposing a video into a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: set of semantically meaningful layers enables a wide range

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of applications, including video editing [5, 23, 25, 45], mo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion re-timing [35], view synthesis [43, 67], game decon-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: struction [46], and obstruction removal [2, 3, 33]. Our work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: focuses on synthesizing fully-visible layers of individual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: objects and their associated effects from a video.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Video Matting with Associated Effects. Omnimatte [35,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 36], inspired by early flow-based methods [1, 9, 51], lever-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages motion cues to decompose a video into RGBA matte

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layers, each comprising an object and its associated effects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It assumes a static background, modeled by planar homo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: graphies, and groups the time-varying residual (moving ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jects and effects) into foreground layers through a test-time

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimization step. Recent works extend Omnimatte by en-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hancing the deep image priors [19, 37] and relaxing the pla-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nar homography constraint to non-rigid warping [35, 59]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or 3D scene representations [29, 47]. However, these ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proaches are limited to restrictive motion assumptions (e.g.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: static backgrounds, accurate pose estimation) and lack gen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: erative capabilities and semantic understanding for com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pleting occluded areas and detecting precise object-effect

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: associations (Fig. 2). Our method, in contrast, requires no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: motion assumption and leverages the generative and seman-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tic priors of our object-effect-removal model to obtain a set

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of fully-visible layers with accurately associated effects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Video Generation and Inpainting. Recent advancements

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in diffusion models have significantly improved the capabil-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ities of text-to-video generation. These models [7, 8, 12, 16,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 17, 21, 48, 56, 58, 60, 65] are trained on massive datasets of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video-text pairs, enabling them to generate visually appeal-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing videos from text descriptions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Text-to-video models have been adapted for the task of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inpainting (e.g., [38, 64, 68]), in which they synthesize con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tent in a user-specified mask region, conditioned on the sur-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rounding visual context. While existing video inpainting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: methods [11, 15, 28, 31, 54, 61, 64] are often employed for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object removal, these models cannot handle the effects that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: extend beyond mask boundaries, leaving undesired shadows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and reflections in the output frames (Fig. 3).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Object Effect Removal. Work [13, 32] in video shadow

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: removal focuses specifically on removing cast shadows, but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: does not aim to perform object-shadow association, ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ject removal, or background completion. Recent meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods [4, 53] fine-tune image diffusion models for object and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect removal. However, they are unsuitable for video ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ject removal because they lack temporal coherence when

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: run on individual frames. Moreover, our goal extends be-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: yond object removal; we aim to decompose a video into an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: entire set of omnimattes to enable layer-based video editing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tasks.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Method

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Given an RGB video I and N object masks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our goal is to generate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video layers: a clean-plate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: RGB background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and N foreground RGBA omnimat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , each containing one object and its associated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects (such as shadows or reflections).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Since ground-truth layered video data is scarce, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aim to apply an existing video diffusion model (Sec. 3.1)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with minimal modifications. Large, pretrained video mod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: els have already learned the required associations between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: objects and their effects as part of their generative task

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Sec. 3.3), so we aim to bring out this ability by finetuning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the model with a small dataset of layered videos (Sec. 3.4).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The diffusion model produces RGB (without alpha), and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retraining to produce alpha maps would require a large

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset of RGBA layers [62]. To avoid changing the output

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: space of the model, we employ a two-step process (Fig. 4):

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (1) creation of the clean-plate video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and N “soloed"

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or single-object videos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing only object i and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background, and (2) reconstruction of the foreground layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from the pairs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (Fig. 4). To construct the back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and solo videos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we train a new video object-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effect-removal model, which we dub “Casper"*, guided by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a trimask (Sec. 3.2). We then reconstruct the layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: via

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: test-time optimization (Sec. 3.5).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1. Base Video Diffusion Model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our object-effect-removal model, Casper, builds upon

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the inpainting variant of the video diffusion model, Lu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: miere [7]. Lumiere is a text-to-video generator with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two-stage cascade of pixel-based diffusion models. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: first-stage base model generates an 80-frame video at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 128×128px resolution from a text prompt. The second

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stage, a spatial super-resolution (SSR) model, upsamples

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the output of the base model to 1024× 1024px resolution.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The Lumiere inpainting model [7, 38], finetuned from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the original text-to-video base model, takes two additional

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions: a masked RGB video with zeroed-out inpaint-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing regions and a binary mask video m. The base inpaint-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing model is followed by the same SSR to achieve high-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution quality.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Casper is finetuned from the inpainting model to perform

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object-and-effect removal. While Casper keeps the same

layout_dets.text: 4.4. Applications

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As showcased in Fig. 1 and Fig. 10, our omnimattes enable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a wide range of video editing for users, such as layer inser-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion and replacement. Each layer can also be independently

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: edited with different transformations, stylizations, and time

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: offsets for motion retiming [35]. The edited layers can then

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: be recomposed seamlessly to generate novel videos.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. Discussion and Limitations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our method overcomes the limitations of existing omni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matte approaches by incorporating a finetuned video in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: painting model that performs object and effect removal.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This is achieved by finetuning a pretrained inpainting model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on a small training set, without modifying the architecture

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to generate an additional alpha channel. The RGB outputs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the video model are then used to reconstruct the RGBA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: omnimatte layers using an optimization step.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The finetuned model inherits the original diffusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model's learned prior on natural videos, allowing for strong

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generalization to scenarios not present in the training set

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 11. Limitations. (a) Casper effectively removes objects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and their associated shadows and reflections, while keeping shape

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deformation in the outputs. (b) In challenging multi-object cases,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Casper may struggle to accurately separate individual effects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 12. User-specified trimask. Casper may introduce un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: desired changes to dynamic background elements (e.g., wave de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tails). To mitigate this, users may specify a coarse preservation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: region to merge with the trimasks. The zoomed-in boxes show

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: precise detail preservation in the specified background area.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., human hands in "lego," "cartoon"). However, this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reliance on a data-driven prior can also limit the range of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects the method can handle. For example, since we did

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not include training data capturing physical deformations,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our current model does not remove effects such as bending

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: poles or trampolines (Fig. 11a). However, our ablation ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: periments (Fig. 9) indicate the model responds well to small

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: additions to the training data, suggesting that it may be pos-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sible capture these effects by curating additional data.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We also observed challenging multi-object cases where,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: despite apparently appropriate training data, our model fails

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to correctly remove effects (Fig. 11b). We hypothesize the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model may need to be trained with additional information

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., instance segmentation) to disambiguate objects and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their effects when multiple, very similar objects are present.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Finally, we observe some cases where Casper will asso-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ciate unrelated background effects with a foreground layer,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such as the waves in Fig. 12. Our system allows the user to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modify the trimask to preserve background areas in simple

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cases (Fig. 12, mid). In future work, such lightweight user

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input can be used to enlarge and improve the training set.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We present a new, generative approach to video layer de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: composition. The current method already outperforms pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vious methods based on more limited priors, and will con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tinue to improve as more ground-truth layered video data

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: becomes available and generative video priors gain strength.
